title: (Moses' blessing on the tribes — Hebrew poetry)

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "This is the blessing that Moses the man of God pronounced on the Israelites before his death. He said: 'The Lord came from Sinai and dawned over them from Seir; he shone forth from Mount Paran. He came with myriads of holy ones from the south, from his mountain slopes.'" — Deut 33:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Moses comes to the end of his life, his final act toward the people is not to scold or warn, but to bless. "This is the blessing that Moses the man of God pronounced on the Israelites before his death." What a beautiful way to leave. After all the rebellion he had endured from these people, Moses' parting words are words of blessing. And he begins by lifting their eyes to God — recalling how the Lord came in glory at Sinai, shining forth in majesty.

There is something deeply moving about how Moses chooses to spend his final breath. He wants the people to remember not their failures, but their God — the glorious, majestic Lord who came near to them. His last gift is to point them once more to the greatness of God.

This challenges us in how we leave our own mark on others. Do our lasting words to people tend toward criticism, or toward blessing? Moses shows us the higher way: to bless, to build up, to point people to God. The words we leave with others can be a gift that outlasts us.

And Moses' blessing flows from having seen God's glory. He could bless the people because he had beheld the Lord who shone forth in splendour. We too have seen God's glory — supremely "in the face of Christ" (2 Cor 4:6). Having seen Him, we are freed to bless others. So let your parting words, your daily words, be words of blessing that point people to the glorious God who came near in Jesus.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do my lasting words to others tend toward blessing or criticism?
2. How might beholding God's glory free me to bless those around me?
3. Who could I intentionally bless and point toward God this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are glorious and majestic, and You came near to us in Christ. Free me from a critical spirit, and make my words a blessing to others. Help me point people always to You. Amen.
